newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SQUARE, RATES SOFTER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SQUARE, RATES SOFTER.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term trading rates were quoted largely softer on Wednesday in a market which opened square, dealers said.
With no significant maturities expected to add to liquidity, the central bank did not auction any treasury bills, which were however being traded on the secondary market steadily at 23.15 percent.

Call money was quoted easier at 20 percent from 22 and NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought half a percentage point softer at 25 percent while their selling rate eased to 23.75 from 24.5 percent.
Bank acceptance bills were quoted at 24.5 percent from 25 percent (buying) and sold at 23 percent, down from 24 percent.
